facts.kid: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin set up the mirror panel near the end of their moonwalk.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA Science: Apollo 11 Experiment Still Running (2004), archived copy

facts.kid: The panel holds 100 little corner cubes.
facts.value: 100 cubes; panel about 46 cm square; each cube about 3.8 cm across
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: Earth-Moon System

facts.kid: It needs no power at all.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: Earth-Moon System

facts.kid: Scientists still bounce lasers off it today.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: The Apollo Experiment That Keeps on Giving (2019)

facts.kid: Apollo 14 and Apollo 15 left mirror panels too.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: The Apollo Experiment That Keeps on Giving (2019)

facts.kid: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: The Apollo Experiment That Keeps on Giving (2019)

facts.kid: The Moon is about 385,000 km away on average.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: The Apollo Experiment That Keeps on Giving (2019)

facts.kid: A laser flash takes about 2.5 seconds to reach the mirrors and come back.
facts.value: 2 x 385,000 km / 299,792 km per s = about 2.57 s
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: The Apollo Experiment That Keeps on Giving (2019)
facts.note: Computed from moon-distance and the speed of light.

facts.kid: Eagle's bottom half stayed on the Moon and worked as the launch pad for the trip home.
facts.note: Find a NASA page.

facts.kid: A seismometer listened for moonquakes.
facts.note: Find a NASA or LPI page on the Passive Seismic Experiment.

facts.kid: On Apollo 15 the rover drove 27.8 km in about 3 hours of driving.
facts.value: 27.8 km in 3 h 2 min; longest trip 12.5 km; farthest 5.0 km from the lander
facts.sourceTitle: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.kid: Its wheels were woven from zinc-coated steel wire, with titanium chevrons for grip.
facts.value: 81.8 cm across, 23 cm wide; chevrons cover 50% of the contact area
facts.sourceTitle: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle
facts.note: Also Smithsonian NASM wheel: https://airandspace.si.edu/collection-objects/wheel-lunar-rover/nasm_A19750830000 (the chevron pattern kept the wheels from sinking into soft soil).

facts.kid: The rover first rolled out on the Moon on July 31, 1971.
facts.note: Secondary source only. Confirm in the Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Journal.

facts.kid: Dave Scott and Jim Irwin drove the Apollo 15 rover.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA Apollo 15 page.

facts.kid: On the first drive the front steering didn't work, so they steered with the rear wheels.
facts.note: Secondary source only. Confirm in the Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Journal.

facts.kid: The rover's tracks can be seen from orbit.
facts.note: Find the LROC featured image of the Apollo 15 site.

facts.kid: Opportunity landed at Meridiani Planum on Mars.
facts.value: January 25, 2004 (UTC); January 24 in US Pacific time
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA/JPL mission page.

facts.kid: It was planned to work for 90 Martian days.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA/JPL: Six things to know about NASA's Opportunity Mars rover (2019), reprint on Phys.org

facts.kid: It kept working for more than 14 years.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA/JPL: Six things to know about NASA's Opportunity Mars rover (2019), reprint on Phys.org

facts.kid: It drove 45.16 km, farther than a marathon.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA/JPL: Six things to know about NASA's Opportunity Mars rover (2019), reprint on Phys.org

facts.kid: It found tiny hematite balls nicknamed "blueberries" that formed with water.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA/JPL: Six things to know about NASA's Opportunity Mars rover (2019), reprint on Phys.org

facts.kid: Its last message came during a planet-wide dust storm.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA/JPL page.

facts.kid: NASA kept calling for months, then said goodbye.
facts.value: mission declared complete February 13, 2019; more than 1,000 recovery commands
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA/JPL page.

facts.kid: Wind sometimes blew dust off its solar panels.
facts.note: Find a NASA/JPL page.

facts.kid: It bounced inside airbags and rolled into a small crater.
facts.note: Find a NASA/JPL page.

facts.kid: The famous line "My battery is low and it's getting dark" was a person's poetic version of its data, not words the rover sent.
facts.note: Do not use until confirmed. Find a reliable source (news fact-check or NASA statement).

facts.kid: Sunsets on Mars look blue near the Sun.
facts.note: Find a NASA image page (Photojournal).

facts.kid: Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA APPEL: NASA's Ingenuity Rotorcraft Makes Final Landing on Mars (2024)

facts.kid: It carries a tiny piece of the 1903 Wright Flyer's wing fabric.
facts.value: wrapped around a cable under its solar panel
facts.sourceTitle: JPL PIA24434: The Wright Brothers
facts.note: Also NASA APPEL: https://appel.nasa.gov/2024/02/23/nasas-ingenuity-rotorcraft-makes-final-landing-on-mars/

facts.kid: It was planned for about 5 flights in 30 days.
facts.note: Secondary sources quoting NASA's January 2024 briefing. Confirm on a NASA page.

facts.kid: It flew 72 times, more than 2 hours in all, 14 times farther than planned.
facts.value: 72 flights; more than 2 h; 14x planned distance
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Team Says Goodbye ... for Now (April 16, 2024)
facts.note: Reprint: https://phys.org/news/2024-04-nasa-ingenuity-mars-helicopter-team.html

facts.kid: Its last flight damaged its rotor blades.
facts.value: final flight January 18, 2024; mission ended January 25, 2024
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Team Says Goodbye ... for Now (April 16, 2024)

facts.kid: It stays at "Valinor Hills" and keeps saving data for future visitors. Its memory could hold about 20 years of daily data.
facts.sourceTitle: JPL: NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Team Says Goodbye ... for Now (April 16, 2024)

facts.kid: Each day it wakes up, takes a picture and records the temperature.
facts.note: Secondary source. Confirm on the JPL page.

facts.kid: It weighs about as much as a bag of sugar.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA page.

facts.kid: Its first flight lasted 39 seconds at Wright Brothers Field.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA page.

facts.kid: Mars air is very thin, about 1% as dense as Earth's.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA Ingenuity page.

facts.kid: Its blades spin very fast to make enough lift.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA Ingenuity page.

facts.kid: Voyager 1 launched in 1977.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA/JPL Voyager page.

facts.kid: It left the Sun's bubble and entered interstellar space.
facts.note: Confirm on a NASA/JPL Voyager page.

facts.kid: Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: its signals take a whole day to reach us.
facts.value: November 18, 2026, 12:16:07 a.m. CST (06:16:07 UTC); about 25.9 billion km (16.1 billion mi), 173.14 AU
facts.sourceTitle: EarthSky: Voyager 1 will be 1 light-day from Earth (citing NASA's June 17, 2026 statement)
facts.note: Secondary sources. Also IFLScience (confirmed with the Voyager team): https://iflscience.com/its-official-voyager-1-will-cross-the-1-light-day-threshold-on-november-18-2026-82733 . Find the NASA/JPL primary page.

facts.kid: Voyager 2 won't reach one light-day until around 2035.
facts.sourceTitle: EarthSky: Voyager 1 will be 1 light-day from Earth (citing NASA's June 17, 2026 statement)
facts.note: Secondary source.

facts.kid: Each Voyager carries a Golden Record with greetings in 55 languages, pictures, music and sounds of Earth.
facts.value: 12-inch gold-plated copper disk; 55 languages; 115 images; committee chaired by Carl Sagan
facts.sourceTitle: The Planetary Society: The Voyager Golden Record
facts.note: Secondary source. Confirm on NASA's Golden Record page.

facts.kid: Surveyor 3 is the only robot probe people have visited on another world. Apollo 12 landed within walking distance.
facts.sourceTitle: Space.com / collectSPACE: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3 parts, 50 years on
facts.note: Secondary source. Confirm on NASA.

facts.kid: The astronauts brought back its camera and other parts so engineers could study how they aged on the Moon.
facts.value: more than 80 researchers studied the parts
facts.sourceTitle: Space.com / collectSPACE: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3 parts, 50 years on
facts.note: Secondary source.

facts.kid: A famous claim that germs survived on the camera was later traced to likely contamination on Earth.
facts.sourceTitle: Space.com / collectSPACE: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3 parts, 50 years on
facts.note: Secondary source.

facts.kid: Sojourner, the first rover on Mars, worked 83 days on a mission planned for 7.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA Science: Pathfinder Sol 8

facts.kid: It used laser stripes to spot hazards.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA Science: Pathfinder Sol 8

facts.kid: Apollo 11 landed at Tranquility Base, close to the middle of the Moon's near side.
facts.deeper: Lunar Module at 0.67416 degrees N, 23.47314 degrees E (planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421), measured from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter images.
facts.sourceTitle: NSSDCA: Apollo Landing Site Coordinates
facts.note: Table row: Lunar Module 0.67416 23.47314 (degrees N latitude, degrees E longitude).

facts.kid: Apollo 15 landed at Hadley-Apennine, beside a long winding valley called Hadley Rille.
facts.deeper: Lunar Module at 26.13239 degrees N, 3.63330 degrees E (planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421).
facts.sourceTitle: NSSDCA: Apollo Landing Site Coordinates
facts.note: Table row: Lunar Module 26.13239 3.63330. Kid wording about the rille is not from this page; confirm before use.

facts.kid: Opportunity came to rest in a small crater on the plains of Meridiani Planum, near the Mars equator.
facts.deeper: 1.946 degrees S, 354.473 degrees E (IAU 2000 body-centered), which is 5.527 degrees W.
facts.sourceTitle: NSSDCA: Opportunity spacecraft details
facts.note: Quote: The spacecraft came to rest in a 20 m diameter crater at 1.946 S and 354.473 E (IAU 2000 body-centered coordinates).

facts.kid: Ingenuity flew in Jezero Crater on Mars.
facts.sourceTitle: NASA Mars 2020 helicopter waypoints data feed
facts.note: Flight 72 record, Sol 1036. The press kit gives about 18 N, 77 E for Jezero: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/mars_2020/landing/mission/landing_site/ . Confirm a prose NASA page before use.
